introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2022, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Plusieurs clés sont raisonnées mais discutables, à relire par un enseignant de Commerce : 2 (manufacturing retenu, industry est plus large), 8 (breaking bulk est un service au détaillant et non au fabricant, alors que prompt payments est parfois cité à tort comme exception), 11 (savings retenu plutôt que contributions), 18 (EX-SHIP retenu comme la cotation où le vendeur supporte le plus de transport), 41 (fixed assets ratio retenu comme n'étant pas un outil ; funding est un outil classique des manuels britanniques), 47 (seule option qui donne le nom complet du département).

Fautes d'impression du sujet conservées dans les options ou énoncés : « coins-operated », « 80,000CFAF », « Giving that », « Mortgage loan » sans point. La question 16 fournit 80,000 CFAF de dépenses qui ne servent pas au calcul (distracteur).

Question 30 : l'énoncé (« rate of exchange between exports and imports ») est maladroit ; clé a (terms of trade) retenue, d (exchange rate) est le piège. Question 4 : « production process ends with » lu comme « la chaîne de production s'achève avec le consommateur ».
Tous les calculs (questions 16, 28, 44) ont été recalculés avec Python.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 25. 25 : les options a, c et d sont toutes des avantages des conteneurs (clé visée c, reduce pilfering).

questions.enonce_markdown: Commerce is sub-divided into;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Commerce is the part of business that moves goods from the producer to the consumer. It has two branches: **trade** (buying and selling: home trade, foreign trade, wholesale and retail) and **aids to trade** (the services that help trade to take place: banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication and advertising). Options A, B and D each name only some aids to trade and leave out one of the two branches.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A dress maker can be classified under;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A dress maker takes raw materials (cloth, thread) and turns them into finished goods (dresses). Making goods from raw materials is **manufacturing** (secondary production). Tertiary production and direct services supply services, not goods. Industry is a wider word that also covers extraction and construction, so manufacturing is the most precise classification.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A company with name ending "PLC" signifies;
questions.corrige_markdown:
PLC means **Public Limited Company**: a company whose shares may be offered to the general public and whose shareholders have limited liability. A public corporation is set up by the state and does not carry the letters PLC, and a private company ends with "Ltd" or "Limited".

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The production process ends with;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Production is complete only when the goods reach the person who uses them. The chain is manufacturer, wholesaler, retailer, **consumer**. The manufacturer starts the chain and the wholesaler and retailer are middlemen in the middle of it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An advert made by radio is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A radio message reaches a very large audience at the same time, so it is **mass advertising** (mass media: radio, television, newspapers). Persuasive and competitive advertising describe the aim of the message, not the medium used, and indirect advertising does not name the product openly.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cash at bank, cash in hand and debtors can be classified as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cash at bank, cash in hand and debtors are assets that are cash or will turn into cash within a short time (less than one year). They are **current assets**. Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities (a difference, not a class of asset), and fixed assets such as land and machines are kept for long-term use.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used to correct errors of an undercharged invoice is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the seller charged too little on an invoice, the buyer owes more money, so the seller sends a **debit note** for the extra amount. A credit note does the opposite: it corrects an overcharge or records returned goods. A delivery note and an advice note do not correct amounts.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Wholesalers perform the following functions to manufacturers EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Services of the wholesaler to the **manufacturer** include buying in large quantities, bearing part of the risks of storage and price change, giving market information and paying promptly (so the manufacturer gets money early). **Breaking bulk** (dividing large quantities into small lots) is a service to the **retailer**, not to the manufacturer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document usually issued by a seller who doubts the credit ability of a new buyer is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **pro forma invoice** looks like an invoice but is not a demand for payment: it asks the new buyer to pay in advance before the goods are sent, because the seller is not sure the buyer will pay later. A credit note and a statement of account are issued to known customers, and a promissory note is written by the debtor.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of coins-operated facility to sell goods is a form of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A machine that releases goods when coins are inserted is an **automatic vending machine** (for example a drinks or snacks machine). Arm-chair shopping and mail order are done from home, and a supermarket is a self-service shop.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main source of capital for a credit union is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A credit union is a co-operative society of savers. Members pool their **savings** and the union lends this money to members who need loans at a low interest rate. Bank loans and government subventions are only occasional sources. Options A and D are close in meaning, but the money a credit union lends comes from members' savings (their savings deposits and share savings).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A marketing method intended to maintain public confidence is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Public relations** aims to build and keep a good image and the trust of the public (for example by sponsoring events, press releases, open days). Sales promotion and advertising aim at increasing sales, and personal selling is face-to-face selling.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document that grants title to goods in international trade is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **bill of lading** is issued by the shipping company. It is a receipt for the goods, a contract of carriage and a **document of title**: the holder is the owner who can claim the goods at the destination port. A certificate of origin only states where goods were made, a bill at sight is a payment order and a certificate of insurance proves cover.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Government assistance to infant industries is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A new (infant) industry is helped by the government with money grants called **subsidies**, so that it can reduce its costs and grow. Embargo, customs duty and quota restrict imports; they protect but are not assistance in the form of money support.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Shops spread all over a town or country with identical buildings are called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Multiple shops** (chain stores) are branches of one firm, with the same appearance, goods and prices, in many places. A department store is one large shop with many departments and a supermarket or hypermarket is one large self-service shop.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Giving that opening stock is 50,000 CFAF, closing stock 20,000 CFAF and expenses 80,000CFAF. Calculate average stock.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Average stock = (opening stock + closing stock) / 2 = $(50\,000 + 20\,000) / 2 = 70\,000 / 2 = 35\,000$ CFAF. The expenses (80,000 CFAF) are not used. Trap: 70,000 is the sum before dividing by 2.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Prompt payments for goods bought by customers will attract a;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **cash discount** is a reduction in price allowed to a buyer who pays quickly, within the period stated by the seller. A quantity discount is for buying large amounts and a trade discount is given to traders, whatever the speed of payment.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A price quotation for which the seller is responsible for cost of transportation is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
With FAS (free alongside ship), FOB (free on board) and FOR (free on rail) the seller pays only up to the quayside, the ship or the railway wagon, and the buyer pays the rest of the transport. With **EX-SHIP** the seller delivers the goods at the destination port, so the seller bears the cost of transporting them all the way (sea freight included). Quotations are read according to the point where the seller's responsibility for transport ends, so EX-SHIP covers the most of it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is NOT an advantage of road transport?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Road transport gives door-to-door delivery (no transshipment), is flexible and is easily available. **Being slow over long distances** is a disadvantage, so it is the answer to a question asking for what is not an advantage.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It is readily available and flexible.

questions.enonce_markdown: The transfer of a public enterprise from the state to the private sector is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Privatization** is the sale or transfer of state-owned enterprises to private owners. Nationalization is the opposite (private to state), a takeover is the purchase of one company by another and para-statals are state-owned enterprises themselves.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Money paid by the insured to cover a risk is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **premium** is the price the insured pays to the insurer for cover. A claim is the request for compensation, the indemnity is the compensation paid after a loss and the surrender value is the money paid when a life policy is cancelled.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the oldest function of commercial banks?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first function of banks, since the goldsmiths who kept customers' gold safe, is **accepting deposits** (safe-keeping of money). Granting loans came from using the deposits, and the other services developed later.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The business unit that requires a certificate of trading to start operations is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A public company first receives a certificate of incorporation, but it may begin business only after obtaining a **certificate of trading** (trading certificate), which shows that the minimum share capital has been subscribed. A partnership and a private company can start with only their agreement or incorporation, and a public corporation is created by law.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a contract of transportation of goods, the consignor is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **consignor** is the person who sends the goods, normally the seller. The consignee is the receiver (buyer) and the carrier or transporter moves the goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Containers are generally good for the transportation of goods because they;

*Options as printed:* A) Can be reused.   B) Are expensive.   C) Reduce pilfering.   D) Ensure maximum safety.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Containers are strong, locked metal boxes of standard size. Goods inside are protected from theft (pilfering), damage and weather, they are quick to load and the boxes can be reused many times. Option B is a disadvantage. Options A, C and D are all advantages, so the printed question does not point to a single best answer (the most likely intended answer is C, reduce pilfering).

**Intended answer: C (Reduce pilfering).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The sharing of profits and losses in an unincorporated business is stated in;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A partnership is unincorporated. The partners write their agreement, including how profits and losses are shared, in a **deed of partnership**. The articles and memorandum of association and the certificate of incorporation belong to incorporated companies.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Holders of fixed deposits accounts are issued;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Money placed in a fixed deposit account is locked for an agreed period, so no cheque is written on it. The bank gives the depositor a **certificate of deposit** as proof of the sum and the term. Cheque books go with current accounts and pass books with savings accounts.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock. It is the cost of the goods that were actually sold during the period. Turnover and net sales refer to sales, and rate of turnover is a ratio.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent in the commodity market who sells to the highest bidder is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **auctioneer** sells goods publicly to the person who offers the highest price (the highest bidder). A forwarding agent arranges transport, a factor holds goods in his own possession and sells them, and a del credere agent guarantees the buyer's payment.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The rate of exchange between a country's exports and her imports is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **terms of trade** compare the price of what a country exports with the price of what it imports (how many imports one unit of exports can buy). The balance of trade is the difference in value between exports and imports, the balance of payments records all money flows with other countries and the exchange rate is the price of one currency in another.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used for the carriage of goods using a hired means of transport is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **consignment note** is made out by the sender (consignor) when goods are given to a hired carrier, mainly road or rail, and it lists the goods and the delivery address. A bill of lading is for sea transport, an airway bill for air transport and a bill of exchange is a payment document, not a transport document.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first to receive benefits during profits sharing in a public company are;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Preference shareholders are paid a fixed dividend **before** the ordinary (equity) shareholders, who receive what is left. (Debenture holders are creditors who receive interest, not a share of profits.) Ordinary shareholders and equity holders are the same people.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An insurance agent who determines premiums of insurance policies is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **actuary** uses statistics and probability to calculate the risk and so the premiums. An assessor or adjuster examines claims after a loss, and a broker arranges policies between clients and insurers.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A current account holder wishing to borrow for 3 weeks is advised to request for;
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **overdraft** lets a current account holder withdraw more than the balance for a short time, and interest is paid only on the amount and period used, which suits a 3-week need. A bank loan or mortgage loan is for longer terms with fixed repayments, and a bank draft is a means of payment, not borrowing.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a deliberate loss in marine insurance?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **general average** loss the captain deliberately sacrifices part of the cargo or ship (for example throwing goods overboard) to save the ship and the rest of the cargo; all owners then share the loss. Total loss, partial loss and particular average loss are accidental losses.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document that serves as a reply to a letter of enquiry is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A buyer sends a letter of enquiry to ask for prices and terms. The seller replies with a **quotation** that states the prices, discounts and delivery terms. An order comes from the buyer after the quotation, and an invoice is sent with the goods.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an advantage of advertising?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Advertising informs and persuades people to buy, so it **increases sales** of the product. The other options are disadvantages or the opposite of what advertising aims at (it increases awareness, not unawareness).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Net profits plus working expenses is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gross profit (gross margin) = net profit + working (operating) expenses, because net profit is what remains of the gross profit after the expenses are paid. Mark-up and net profit margin are percentages, not this sum.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cheques rejected for payments by banks on grounds of duration are;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque is valid for a limited time (usually six months from its date). After this time the bank refuses it and it is called a **stale cheque**. Crossed, ordered and counter cheques are types of cheques that are not refused because of age.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Selling Cameroon's cocoa cheaper in the Japanese market than in Cameroon is an example of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Selling goods abroad at a price lower than the price in the home market (sometimes lower than the cost) is **dumping**. Smuggling is illegal entry or exit of goods, and price discrimination is charging different prices to different customers; the question describes the export case, dumping.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is NOT a monetary policy tool?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Monetary policy tools are the means used by the central bank to control the money supply: open market operations (buying and selling securities), special deposits that banks must place with the central bank, funding (changing the structure of government debt from short to long term) and reserve or liquidity ratios. A **fixed assets ratio** is not one of them: it is only a ratio in a firm's accounts.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main objective of a consumer protection law is to check;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Consumer protection laws aim to prevent consumers from being **exploited** (high prices, false weights, false description, unsafe goods). Substandard goods are one case, but the general main objective is the protection of consumers against exploitation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A specialized ship for the transportation of perishables is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Perishable goods (fish, meat, fruit) need cold storage during the voyage, so they travel in a **refrigerator ship** (reefer). Coastal liners follow fixed routes along the coast, tramps have no fixed route and passenger liners carry people.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that opening stock = 35,000 CFAF, purchases = 50,000 CFAF and closing stock = 15,000 CFAF; calculate cost of goods sold.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock $= 35\,000 + 50\,000 - 15\,000 = 70\,000$ CFAF. Traps: 85,000 CFAF is opening stock plus purchases (the goods available for sale) and 65,000 CFAF is obtained by adding the closing stock in the wrong direction.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A questionnaire to be filled before an insurance policy is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The person who wants insurance first completes a **proposal form** giving full and true details of the risk (utmost good faith). The insurer uses it to decide whether to accept and at what premium. A cover note is temporary proof of cover, the policy is the contract and a claim form is used after a loss.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The excess of the value of exports over the value of imports is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
When exports are worth more than imports the balance of trade is in surplus, called a **favourable balance of trade**. Terms of trade are a price ratio, not a value difference.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A government institution that ensures that consumers are not exploited with high prices is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The government department that fixes and checks prices and checks that weights and measures used by traders are correct is the **Price Control, Weights and Measures department**. Option C gives its complete name, while A, B and D are incomplete.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Price control, weights and measures department.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are the social responsibilities of an enterprise EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Social responsibilities are things a firm does for the community on its own initiative: recreation, health centres and social schemes. **Paying taxes** is a legal duty required by law, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Payment of taxes to the state.

questions.enonce_markdown: A reward to a man-made resource of an enterprise is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A man-made resource is **capital** (machines, buildings, tools). The reward to capital is **interest**. Profit rewards the entrepreneur, salary rewards labour and rent rewards land.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank facility that enables customers to withdraw money 24/7 is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **ATM** (automatic teller machine) gives cash at any hour with a card and a PIN. A night safe is for depositing takings after closing, and a standing order and a direct debit are instructions to pay money regularly.

**Answer: B.**
